chapter: Technique and life on the road (repeated passages)
title: Where his plunger style came from
summary: He heard plunger playing from Ellington and Joe Smith in Fletcher Henderson's band, and thinks Johnny Dunn used it.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: For instance the way you use the plunger is pretty unique I think. When did you start doing that?

Oh, I've been doing that for years. I used to hear bands from way back -- well one band in particular was Duke Ellington's band. No, Fletch Henderson too had a plunger player -- he had Joe Smith who played plunger but

he played sweet horn. He was one of my idols. Just like Bobbie Hackett, they seemed to be the same type of guys you know -- in the way that they were trained -- the solos they played. You know -- they played pretty you know. And I liked Joe Smith very much.
And come to think of it I think I'm -- I think a guy named of -- oh, what was his name -- not Bubba Myer (PHONETIC) -- there was a guy before Bubba Myer (PHONETIC) What was his name?
I think he used a lot of plunger then.
